text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Next year's pension increase will not be lower than the net wage increase of the previous year, Prime Minister Gyula Horn said.
- Parliament continued a general debate on a judicial reform yesterday.
- Socialist Party parliamentary group leader Imre Szekeres clashed with Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan in a much publicized debate at Jaszapati, central Hungary, Thursday evening.
- The Democratic Forum has suggested that the major newscasts on public service radio and television cover church-related events for up to several minutes on each and every broadcast.
- The leadership of the Socialist Party parliamentary group proposed Jozsef Rooz, Gyorgy Naszvadi or Elemer Tertak, in that order, for the post of president of the State Audit Office.
The European Union is granting 40 million ECUs for regional development in Hungary this year, EU commissioner Michael Bursich announced in Nyiregyhaza yesterday.
- The National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) Thursday finalized a tender launched for entitlement to broadcast national commercial radio programs.
- About $36.7 million will be invested in the Ford vehicle parts production plant in Szekesfehervar, Ford Hungary plans to invest $36.7 million into expanding its Szekesfehervar plant.
- The southeast Hungarian electricity supplier Demasz Rt. generated a Ft 5 million profit last year, emerging as the only profitable company of its kind in the country.
- The British store chain Tesco will build a 20-25,000 sqm shopping mall in Nyiregyhaza, northeast Hungary by 1999 at the latest.

- Although economic growth has started, its sustainability is not yet certain, agreed Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and National Bank president Gyorgy Suranyi at a meeting organized by the Trend/Prognozis Economic Club yesterday.
